source_backed_atoms.extracted_rule: Tight channels are treated like higher-timeframe breakouts; when unclear, trade only with the trend.
source_backed_atoms.implementation_hint: Use higher-timeframe breakout context and block counter-trend entries in tight-channel state.

source_backed_atoms.extracted_rule: A tight/small-pullback trend has shallow pullbacks, often 1-3 bars, and pullbacks smaller than about two average bars or two to three minimum scalps.
source_backed_atoms.implementation_hint: Approximate with pullback depth, pullback bar count, average bar size, and trend-direction persistence.

source_backed_atoms.extracted_rule: After 20 or more bars above the moving average, the first pullback to the average or first close below it can become a trend-continuation reversal entry.
source_backed_atoms.implementation_hint: Model as first MA test or first opposite-side close after a sustained trend gap-bar run.

source_backed_atoms.extracted_rule: Correct stops can be far in strong trends; strong traders use wider stops below the last trend leg and trail after new extremes.
source_backed_atoms.implementation_hint: Keep position sizing tied to stop distance instead of tightening stops to fit a fixed quantity.

source_backed_atoms.extracted_rule: A strong trend can reverse, but it needs stronger contrary evidence such as wedge/MAG failure, all trend-continuation setups failing, and opposite breakout with follow-through.
source_backed_atoms.implementation_hint: Require explicit opposite breakout/follow-through before treating tight-channel continuation as failed.

source_review_answers.answer: Tightness is defined by tradeability and pullback size: higher-timeframe breakout behavior, pullbacks around 1-3/1-4 bars, smaller than about two average bars or two to three minimum scalps, and poor counter-trend profitability.

Continuation weakens when gaps close, pullbacks overlap breakout points, the market shifts toward broad-channel/TR behavior, or opposite breakout/follow-through appears after failed continuation setups.
Pullback depth/count, average bar size, MA tests, gap bars, and opposite breakout/follow-through are OHLCV-approximable; channel-quality and example matching still require visual review.

source_backed_atoms.extracted_rule: A climax is a late move-ending breakout; most climaxes lead first to a 3-10 bar trading range, not automatically to a new opposite trend.
source_backed_atoms.implementation_hint: Mark late-trend acceleration as decision-zone context, not immediate reversal permission.

source_backed_atoms.extracted_rule: After about 10-20 or 20+ bars, a large trend bar near support/resistance can be either measuring gap or exhaustion gap; follow-through and gap closure decide the label.
source_backed_atoms.implementation_hint: Track late trend age, large-body rank, gap/overlap state, and next-bar follow-through before assigning reversal state.

source_backed_atoms.extracted_rule: After exhaustion, early counter-trend entries have better reward/risk but lower probability; waiting for strong opposite breakout raises probability with worse reward/risk.
source_backed_atoms.implementation_hint: Split future spec into early visual-review entry and confirmed opposite-breakout entry; do not merge them into one trigger.

source_backed_atoms.extracted_rule: Consecutive sell climaxes often imply TBTL or trading range, but a final 5-10 bar sell vacuum can still appear before the larger correction.
source_backed_atoms.implementation_hint: Require TBTL tracking and allow a final-climax exception before promoting reversal evidence.

source_backed_atoms.extracted_rule: Strong micro-channel pressure means the first reversal can fail; final buy climax can still resolve roughly 50/50 between reversal and trend resumption.
source_backed_atoms.implementation_hint: Block promotion unless visual review confirms failed breakout/exhaustion rather than measuring-gap trend continuation.

source_review_answers.answer: The reviewed sources support late-trend acceleration, exhaustion gap, failed breakout, TBTL, support/resistance, and final-flag language, but final-flag classification remains visual-first.

A climax alone is not enough. Confirmation needs follow-through failure, gap closure or negative gap, support/resistance reaction, or a strong opposite breakout depending on early-versus-confirmed entry route.

Late trend age, bar count, large-body rank, gaps, follow-through, and TBTL tracking are OHLCV-approximable; wedge/final flag, exhaustion versus measuring-gap interpretation, and failed-breakout quality require visual review.
